statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-35191 ("QUIC Unvalidated Amplification Credit may be Over Accounted", Low): an OpenSSL QUIC server configured not to perform address validation adds the length of a whole received datagram to its unvalidated credit once for every QUIC packet in that datagram, so a peer sending datagrams that hold several packets makes the server exceed the RFC 9000 limit of three times the data received, and a spoofing attacker could use the server to amplify a denial-of-service attack. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9; the FIPS modules are not affected because the QUIC stack is outside the FIPS module boundary. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/0fe4442d4f8ea3af8a174046dae176e0d4717239, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.9. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, DSA-6531-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-35191. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-35191. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The fix moves the unvalidated-credit accounting from ossl_quic_handle_frames(), which runs once per packet, to port_default_packet_handler(), which runs once per datagram. In the disassembly of libssl, located with the shipped debug symbols, port_default_packet_handler() calls ossl_quic_tx_packetiser_add_unvalidated_credit() and ossl_quic_handle_frames() does not in every build from the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 on, FIPS builds included, and the reverse holds in every earlier build, on both architectures (debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build). Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the QUIC stack outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libssl is Debian's 3.5 library checked above.
